header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Agenda: weekly POC sync — model curation, pinning policy, rollback playbook, action items
Attendees: see metadata
summary: Quick progress sync on model selection for the pilot. Reviewed benchmark outliers, discussed pinning strategy to minimize regressions, walked through a proposed rollback/drill process and shadow routing plan. Customer raised concerns about p95 latency on long-sequence prompts and KMS integration for private telemetry. Agreed on concrete next steps: share a detailed latency/cost matrix, provide rollback runbook draft, and schedule a live rollback drill next week.
topics: Model candidate comparison across sequence-length buckets
Pinning policy: hard pin vs soft pin with percent-based rollouts
Shadow routing and canary -> rollback choreography
Security: KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2 notes
Next steps: benchmarks, samples, live drill
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, let's kick off. I see we've got about 50 minutes, goal is narrow: align on which model variants to keep pinned for the pilot and rehearse the rollback path.
[00:18] Leah (BrightLane): Great, yeah I'll try to be concise, main thing yesterday we ran the new prompts and saw some spikes at the p95 for longer sequences, so want to understand which models behave.
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood SE): Quick context — we ran the three model candidates: rwd-3b-opt, rwd-7b-quant, and a larger rwd-13b-16k variant, each with different KV cache and quantization knobs. The sheet I shared shows p50/p95 per seq-length bucket (128/512/2048).
[00:52] Marco (Customer Eng): Right, and on the 2048 tests we saw p95 around 2.4s on 13b but with big variance — sometimes spikes to 3.8s. Not sure if it's batching or cache misses.
[01:07] Jordan: Could be prefix cache thrash, especially when the prompt distribution is high-cardinality. Did you run with prefix caching on?
[01:15] Tom (BrightLane ML): We left prefix caching off for that run because we were profiling raw latencies.
[01:20] Jordan: Ah okay, that explains it, because with caching on the 13b p95 drops to ~1.6s in our repro. But, caching has warm-up effects on cold starts.
[01:32] Samir: So two tradeoffs here: cost + latency midsized vs steady-state vs cold-start behavior. For pilot we recommend pinning the 7b-quant as default for user-facing low-latency flows and keep 13b pinned behind a slow-path for high-quality tasks.
[01:45] Priya (Security): Quick security note — any plan where we move traffic between variants has to be logged end-to-end and the KMS envelope keys for telemetry must be vetted. We need an answer on whether Redwood can integrate with our HashiCorp Vault KMS.
[01:58] Maya (Redwood SE): Yes, we support Vault KMS via our Private deployment connectors — there's a config doc, I can add specific steps to the runbook.
[02:08] Leah: Can you also include how audit logs look? Our compliance team cares about token-level traces — but they want redacted content in logs.
[02:18] Jordan: We typically write meta + usage metrics to the console and you can opt-in for sampling of full text with redaction rules. I'll include examples.
[02:27] Marco: Back to rollback — show me a simple flow: we pin 7b, start a canary with 5% to 13b for quality, then if quality dips we roll back to 7b, correct?
[02:37] Samir: That's the idea. But we recommend a two-stage canary: 5% shadow for 24h, then a 10% live canary (non-blocking) with guardrails. If p95 increases more than 20% or regression in eval prompts, auto-rollback triggers.
[02:50] Tom: Auto-rollback triggers sound good; who owns the playbook? For example, what if the auto-rollback fails due to capacity constraints?
[02:59] Jordan: Good question — the runbook has an escape hatch: fallback to a degraded model variant (smaller quantized instance) or route to fallback region. Also alerts go to on-call and to the AE.
[03:09] Leah: Can we do a drill so we validate rollback paths?
[03:12] Samir: Yes — we proposed a live rollback drill 2026-01-15. Jordan will run the scenario with Marco and Tom to make sure traffic routing and backend switches are smooth.
[03:23] [Speaker 1]: (muffled) I can join the drill.
[03:30] Jordan: I'm going to walk through the draft runbook now — step 1, identify failing metric (p95 or accuracy on golden prompts), step 2, set manual freeze on version gateway, step 3, trigger soft pin to previous model, step 4, confirm telemetry and release.
[03:48] Marco: What's the "freeze" action? Is that manually flipping a boolean in our console?
[03:53] Jordan: It's a config flip via API: version gateway receives a hard pin on model id. We also support temporary pin percentages for canary. The console shows active pins, rollback history, and traces.
[04:06] Tom: How fast is the gateway change? Like, near-instant?
[04:10] Jordan: Typically within seconds for routing table updates. The slow part is in-flight requests draining, worst-case few hundred ms to seconds depending on sequence length.
[04:20] Leah: One thing I noticed on the spreadsheet, the cost per 1000 tokens for 13b is much higher — can we get a delta column showing cost impact for traffic splits?
[04:29] Samir: Sure — I'll add a cost-delta column and simulate 5/10/20% split cost implications.
[04:36] Marco: Also can you annotate which models have KV-cache-friendly execution? We saw memory pressure on the big ones when many concurrent sessions.
[04:44] Jordan: Yep, the 7b-quant has more efficient KV packing in our runtime; 13b needs more mem per session. I'll mark that.
[04:52] [00:05:00] Jordan: Now quickly looking at the model comparison — rwd-7b-quant gave best cost/latency for 512 token avg workloads. rwd-13b-16k gives quality lifts on long-form summarization but at higher cost and variance.
[05:15] Priya: On compliance — how do you handle PII or PHI in logs? We need a redaction pipeline and assurances that telemetry doesn't leak PHI.
[05:24] Maya: We can redact at ingestion and also only store hashed identifiers; the Private deployment option gives you control over retention. We'll include the retention settings.
[05:33] Priya: Cool, send that. SOC2 evidence would be nice too.
[05:36] Samir: We'll share the SOC2 summary doc and the connectivity diagram.
[05:40] Tom: Back to rollback — what about shadow routing? Could we shadow 100% to 13b while serving 7b to users to get quality signals without affecting user experience?
[05:49] Jordan: Yes, shadowing is low-risk — we collect side-by-side outputs and run automated evals. We recommend initial shadowing for 48h across representative traffic to compute precision/regression metrics.
[05:59] Leah: Would there be extra cost for shadowing?
[06:02] Samir: Yes, shadowing doubles inference cost for the shadow portion; we'll quantify that in the cost sheet.
[06:07] Marco: We may shadow only a 10% sample to save cost but still have statistical power.
[06:12] Jordan: That's reasonable. Also note, shadowing doesn't count toward traffic quotas if configured as internal.
[06:20] [00:10:00] Samir: Let's talk about pin policy options: hard pin (100% pinned to model id) gives predictability but slows rollouts. Soft pin with percent-based routing gives gradual rollout and easier rollback. We suggest default soft pin with an automatic rollback policy tied to both latency and eval-run regressions.
[06:40] Tom: How do you measure eval-run regressions? We have a golden set of prompts but sampling across different intents is hard.
[06:48] Jordan: We run eval sets comprising your golden prompts plus a sampled set from production. Regression defined as mean decrease in quality score > X% or increase in hallucination indicators. We'll tune the thresholds with you.
[06:59] Leah: What's X?
[07:01] Jordan: Typically 5-10% depending on sensitivity; higher sensitivity for critical features.
[07:08] Marco: For the pilot we want conservative threshold, maybe 8% and a manual review gate before auto-rollback.
[07:15] Samir: Ok we'll propose a config: auto-detect at 20% and alert at 8% so you can choose manual rollback.
[07:26] Priya: For audit we need immutable rollback logs and proof that traffic changed, who approved it etc. Can you surface that?
[07:33] Maya: Yes, our console stores an immutable event stream with actor, timestamp, reason, and pre/post config snapshots. For Private deployments you can ship that to your SIEM.
[07:44] Tom: On the bench infra — are you using dynamic batching? We saw variance that looked like batching windows.
[07:51] Jordan: We use workload-aware continuous batching; it aims to fill tokens while respecting latency SLOs. Batching windows can introduce small p95 blips under high tail latency for long sequences.
[08:03] Marco: Is there a knob to reduce batching to favor latency?
[08:06] Jordan: Yes you can set max batch delay and target latency; increasing cost but lowering latency. We'll include suggested settings per flow.
[08:16] Leah: For the next sprint, Tam wants to lock the model for customer support chat only. How quickly can we pin per-route?
[08:23] Samir: Per-route pinning is supported — you can pin model per route, per API key. Changes propagate in seconds.
[08:28] Leah: Good. We want chat pinned to 7b-quant and long-form summarization pinned to 13b.
[08:34] Samir: Noted. We'll codify that in the pilot config and shadow the summarization route for 48h.
[08:40] [00:20:00] Jordan: Now I'm going to read out items I will add to the runbook: rollback thresholds, manual freeze steps, canary percentages, fallback variant list (7b-quant-lite), telemetry checks, who to call, and required pre-checks (capacity, KV cache warmup).
[08:59] Marco: On failover regions — if West-1 is saturated, do you auto-fail to East-1? We have latency customers so that could be tricky.
[09:06] Jordan: Auto-failover is policy-driven. Default is no auto cross-region fail for low-latency flows, but you can enable it with per-route latency caps.
[09:16] Tom: Let's talk about the 'rollback playback' drill — what will that look like?
[09:20] Samir: We'll simulate a regression: step 1 inject a regression marker into eval set, step 2 watch alert fire, step 3 execute rollback via version gateway, step 4 confirm degraded metrics return to baseline and user-facing telemetry ok. Jordan will orchestrate.
[09:33] Jordan: Also we'll test partial failure: rollback API returns 500 or gateway is out of sync — ensure escape hatch: manual DNS switch or route splitting. We'll rehearse both.
[09:44] Leah: Sounds thorough.
[09:47] Priya: On the security ask: we need to confirm if telemetry ever leaves our VPC for hosted mode.
[09:54] Maya: For Private deployment telemetry stays in your VPC; for hosted we push metrics to Redwood controllers but you can choose redaction and retention. We'll put the exact network flow in the diagram.
[10:04] Marco: One more perf question — when you say 1.6s p95 with caching, is that measured with batch size=1?
[10:10] Jordan: It's mixed; the number reported is for our target concurrency with batching enabled and typical production arrival. We'll give both single-shot and batched numbers.
[10:20] Tom: Can you include a column for tokenization overhead? Our prompts are sometimes pre-tokenized differently in our pipeline.
[10:26] Jordan: Good point — tokenizer mismatch can add latency. We'll add a column showing tokenization cost and a recommended tokenizer alignment.
[10:34] Samir: OK summarizing next steps before we run out of time — Samir to send updated spreadsheet and cost-delta, Jordan to post runbook draft, Maya to post SOC2/connectivity docs, Tom to share prompt samples, Marco & Jordan to schedule rollback drill.
[10:49] Leah: Quick question about fallback: what if we degrade to the smaller quantized variant and it produces quality issues? Do we surface a user-facing message?
[10:58] Jordan: We recommend returning a short fallback message for critical flows and sending a degraded quality flag in metadata for product to treat accordingly.
[11:06] Tom: That works.
[11:09] [00:30:00] Samir: Anything else on model curation?
[11:12] Marco: One ask — can you add a column in the sheet showing which models are compatible with our on-prem hardware if we migrate later?
[11:18] Samir: I'll annotate compatibility notes.
[11:21] Priya: Also please include the data retention configuration examples in the SOC2 doc for legal review.
[11:26] Maya: Will do.
[11:29] Leah: Alright, I'm comfortable with the plan. Let's run the drill and then decide pin percentages after we see shadow results.
[11:37] Samir: Great — we'll schedule the drill and update the docs. Any other blockers?
[11:41] Tom: None from engineering side.
[11:44] Marco: No.
[11:45] Priya: Just timeline on SOC2 doc, please by 2026-01-14.
[11:49] Samir: Noted.
[11:51] Jordan: I'll follow up with the runbook link and a short checklist.
[11:55] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll close and follow up on the action items.
[12:00] [End of recording]

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker mislabels, some words transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "rwd" sometimes as "red"), punctuation may be off.
